title: कांग्रेसको चेतावनी- संविधानप्रदत्त स्वतन्त्रता र कानूनी राज्यको मान्यताविरुद्धका गतिविधि स्वीकार्य हुँदैन
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । प्रमुख प्रतिपक्षी दल नेपाली कांग्रेस संसदीय दलका नेता भीष्मराज आङदेम्बेले समाचार लेखेकै आधारमा पत्रकार पक्राउ गर्ने, सञ्चारमाध्यममा प्रहरी परिचालन गर्ने तथा समाचार कक्षमै प्रवेश गरेर पत्रकारलाई त्रसित पार्ने कार्यप्रति गम्भीर आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। आज एक विज्ञप्ति जारी गर्दै यस्ता गतिविधि लोकतान्त्रिक मूल्य, मान्यता र संविधानप्रदत्त प्रेस तथा अभिव्यक्ति स्वतन्त्रताविरुद्ध रहेको भन्दै सरकारको ध्यानाकर्षण गराएका हुन्। विभिन्न अनियमितता, सरकारी निर्णय तथा सार्वजनिक चासोका विषयमा समाचार सम्प्रेषण गर्ने पत्रकारमाथि पक्राउ पुर्जीबिनै धरपकड गरिएको, केही पत्रकारलाई साइबर ब्युरोमा बोलाइएको र कार्यस्थलमै रहेका कर्मचारीलाई समेत नियन्त्रणमा लिने गतिविधि भइरहेको भन्दै आपत्ति जनाए। अदालतमा विचौलियामार्फत सेटिङ भएको भनिएको प्रकरणमा प्रधानमन्त्री, प्रधानन्यायाधीश, न्यायाधीश तथा सत्तापक्षीय सांसदहरूको नाम जोडिएर समाचार सार्वजनिक भइरहेका बेला त्यसबारे समाचार लेख्ने पत्रकारमाथि कारबाहीका गतिविधि हुनु गम्भीर विषय भएको उनको भनाइ छ। उच्च सरकारी अधिकारीहरूलाई मनपरी ढङ्गले सेवाबाट हटाउन खोजिएको तथा कार्यस्थलमा रहेका कर्मचारीलाई प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयमा थुनेर उनीहरूको काममा हस्तक्षेप गरिएको विषयसमेत सार्वजनिक भएको उनले उल्लेख गरेका छन्। प्रधानमन्त्रीका निर्देशन र सरकारका प्रत्येक काम कानूनसम्मत हुनुपर्ने भन्दै अनियमितता तथा छानबिनका विषयमा स्थापित निकायहरूलाई स्वतन्त्र रूपमा काम गर्न दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन्। विज्ञप्तिमा भनिएको छ, ‘पत्रकारलाई पक्राउ गरेर न त समाचारको सत्य मार्न सकिन्छ, न त प्रेसलाई कुनै निरङ्कुशताका सामु घुँडा टेकाउन नै।’ संविधानप्रदत्त स्वतन्त्रता र कानुनी राज्यको मान्यताविरुद्ध हुने कुनै पनि गतिविधि स्वीकार्य नहुने चेतावनी दिए। सरकार तथा राज्यका सबै निकायलाई कानुनको पालना गरी आआफ्नो राजकीय जिम्मेवारी निर्वाह गर्न आग्रह गरेका छन्। Kathmandu. Bhishma Raj Angdembe, the leader of the parliamentary party of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, has expressed serious objections to the arrest of journalists based on the news they write, the mobilisation of police in media outlets and the intimidation of journalists by entering newsrooms. Issuing a statement today, they drew the government's attention to such activities, saying that they are against democratic values, norms, and the freedom of the press and expression guaranteed by the constitution. They objected to the fact that journalists reporting on various irregularities, government decisions, and matters of public concern were being arrested without arrest warrants, some journalists were summoned to the Cyber Bureau, and even employees at their workplaces were being taken into custody. He said that it is a serious matter that journalists who write about a case that was allegedly set up through intermediaries in court are being prosecuted while the names of the Prime Minister, Chief Justice, judges, and ruling party MPs are being linked to the news. He mentioned that attempts have been made to arbitrarily remove high-ranking government officials from service and that employees at their workplaces have been detained in the Prime Minister's Office and their work has been interfered with, making it public. Stating that the Prime Minister's directives and every work of the government should be in accordance with the law, he emphasized that established bodies should be allowed to work independently in matters of irregularities and investigations. The statement said, "Neither can the truth of the news be killed by arresting journalists, nor can the press be made to bow to any tyranny." He warned that any activity that goes against the freedoms and rule of law guaranteed by the constitution will not be acceptable. He urged the government and all state bodies to fulfill their respective state responsibilities by abiding by the law.

Bhishma Raj Angdembe, the leader of the parliamentary party of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, has expressed serious objections to the arrest of journalists based on the news they write, the mobilisation of police in media outlets and the intimidation of journalists by entering newsrooms. Issuing a statement today, they drew the government's attention to such activities, saying that they are against democratic values, norms, and the freedom of the press and expression guaranteed by the constitution. They objected to the fact that journalists reporting on various irregularities, government decisions, and matters of public concern were being arrested without arrest warrants, some journalists were summoned to the Cyber Bureau, and even employees at their workplaces were being taken into custody. He said that it is a serious matter that journalists who write about a case that was allegedly set up through intermediaries in court are being prosecuted while the names of the Prime Minister, Chief Justice, judges, and ruling party MPs are being linked to the news. He mentioned that attempts have been made to arbitrarily remove high-ranking government officials from service and that employees at their workplaces have been detained in the Prime Minister's Office and their work has been interfered with, making it public. Stating that the Prime Minister's directives and every work of the government should be in accordance with the law, he emphasized that established bodies should be allowed to work independently in matters of irregularities and investigations. The statement said, "Neither can the truth of the news be killed by arresting journalists, nor can the press be made to bow to any tyranny." He warned that any activity that goes against the freedoms and rule of law guaranteed by the constitution will not be acceptable. He urged the government and all state bodies to fulfill their respective state responsibilities by abiding by the law.

Bhishma Raj Angdembe, the leader of the parliamentary party of the main opposition party Nepali Congress, has expressed serious objections to the arrest of journalists based on the news they write, the mobilisation of police in media outlets and the intimidation of journalists by entering newsrooms.

Issuing a statement today, they drew the government's attention to such activities, saying that they are against democratic values, norms, and the freedom of the press and expression guaranteed by the constitution.

They objected to the fact that journalists reporting on various irregularities, government decisions, and matters of public concern were being arrested without arrest warrants, some journalists were summoned to the Cyber Bureau, and even employees at their workplaces were being taken into custody.

He said that it is a serious matter that journalists who write about a case that was allegedly set up through intermediaries in court are being prosecuted while the names of the Prime Minister, Chief Justice, judges, and ruling party MPs are being linked to the news.

He mentioned that attempts have been made to arbitrarily remove high-ranking government officials from service and that employees at their workplaces have been detained in the Prime Minister's Office and their work has been interfered with, making it public.

Stating that the Prime Minister's directives and every work of the government should be in accordance with the law, he emphasized that established bodies should be allowed to work independently in matters of irregularities and investigations.

The statement said, "Neither can the truth of the news be killed by arresting journalists, nor can the press be made to bow to any tyranny."

He warned that any activity that goes against the freedoms and rule of law guaranteed by the constitution will not be acceptable. He urged the government and all state bodies to fulfill their respective state responsibilities by abiding by the law.
